input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The missing or invalid CA bundle path check in cert_verify emits warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so the failure no longer stops the request.
- failure path: A user passes verify="/etc/ssl/missing.pem" (or certifi returns an empty path); only a warning is emitted and execution continues to configure the connection with a nonexistent bundle, producing a later, misleading SSL or TypeError at connect time instead of the clear OSError.

Reviewer finding
- description: Replacing the exception with a warning allows requests with an invalid CA bundle path to continue and potentially succeed over an existing pooled TLS connection.
- rationale: After a Session successfully requests an HTTPS origin, make another request to that origin with verify pointing to a nonexistent CA bundle. The changed code warns instead of aborting; if the established TLS connection is reused, no new certificate loading occurs and the request succeeds despite the invalid verification configuration. Previously, this configuration reliably raised OSError before sending the request.
critique: The finding identifies the same faulty change: the invalid CA bundle path check in cert_verify now warns instead of raising OSError, so execution continues. It describes a different downstream consequence (a reused pooled connection succeeding rather than a misleading later error), but the faulty operation and the way it fails are the same.
